name: António Guterres
role: UN Secretary-General (2017–); Portuguese prime minister (1995–2002); UN High Commissioner for Refugees (2005–2015)
summary: Guterres is a social democrat by background who, as UN Secretary-General, speaks mainly for multilateralism, international law, disarmament, climate action, development finance and human rights. His own statements as Secretary-General are the evidence here; his earlier record as Portuguese prime minister and refugee commissioner was not researched in this pass.

algorithmic-government.rationale: He says humanity's hand must stay firmly in control of technology and presses for human-rights-based AI guardrails and talks on limiting lethal autonomous weapons.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: He urges states to use the Charter's dispute-settlement tools including arbitration and to accept the ICJ's compulsory jurisdiction and comply with its binding decisions.

arms-reduction.rationale: He warns that investment in the tools of war outstrips investment in peace and pushes arms control and disarmament commitments.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: He states that attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are strictly prohibited under international humanitarian law.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He calls for reparatory justice for colonialism and says decolonization left unjust structures in place.

colonial-reparations.rationale: He has called for reparatory justice and reparations for enslavement and colonialism.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He says independent African states inherited a system built to serve others and calls for reparations for colonialism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He urges countries to address racism in all its forms, particularly where it is embedded in laws, policies and institutions.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: In a 2023 message he urged all member states to end the criminalization of consensual same-sex relations ('Being yourself should never be a crime').

death-penalty.rationale: He says he will keep advocating the universal abolition of capital punishment and calls it cruel and ineffective.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: His government created the guaranteed minimum income in 1996 for people in extreme poverty, a benefit later made a universal right.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: He frames the choice as a world of laws against 'might makes right' and invokes the sovereign equality of member states.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He urges countries to address racism in all its forms, particularly where it is embedded in laws, policies and institutions, which rules out discouraging families across racial lines.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He calls climate change the defining issue of the age and demands a 60 per cent emissions cut by 2035 and a fast, fair, funded fossil-fuel phase-out.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He stresses that Security Council decisions can legally bind all member states and asks states to respect binding ICJ rulings, but does not set out enforcement powers in so many words.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He says the rights and dignity of all people must be safeguarded at all times and calls international law a lifeline of equal treatment.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He calls for a worldwide fossil-fuel phase-out with reduction targets for fossil production and for ending fossil subsidies, which is incompatible with allowing new extraction.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: He calls for abolishing executions in all circumstances and decries secret executions, which excludes executing suspects without trial.

force-without-un.rationale: He says the Security Council alone has Charter authority to act for all states on peace and security and lists the illegal use of force among grave violations.

future-generations.rationale: He frames climate inaction as failing the generations to come ('Baby 8 Billion') and champions the Declaration on Future Generations.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: He champions gender parity at the top of the UN and equal participation and leadership of women, though he does not say it should be legally required.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: He ties record heat and the 1.5 degree breach to fossil-fuel emissions and says emissions must peak and fall rapidly.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He holds that total elimination of nuclear weapons is the only guarantee, so no country should hold them.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: He says the only guarantee against use of nuclear weapons is their total elimination and urges nuclear-armed states toward disarmament.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: In his 2021 Indigenous Peoples Day message he said there is no excuse for denying indigenous peoples self-determination and meaningful participation in decisions, and that they have been stripped of political and economic autonomy. This is about indigenous peoples, a narrower case than the statement, so the answer is +1.

multipolar-world.rationale: He calls the increasingly multipolar world positive but warns multipolarity needs effective multilateral institutions.

nation-first.rationale: He asks whether the world will be 'a scramble for self-interest' or one where nations come together, and calls international cooperation hard-headed pragmatism.

party-controls-media.rationale: He lists protecting journalists and freedom of expression, and preserving civic space, among the rights to be chosen.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: He lists unconstitutional changes of government among the violations of international law that set dangerous precedents.

positive-liberty.rationale: He says dignity requires realizing rights through development that ends poverty and hunger and opens education, health and opportunity.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: He urges countries to address racism in all its forms, particularly where it is embedded in laws, policies and institutions, which rules out racial limits on immigration.

racial-franchise.rationale: He urges countries to address racism in all its forms, particularly where it is embedded in laws, policies and institutions, which rules out restricting the vote to one ethnic group.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He urges countries to address racism in all its forms, particularly where it is embedded in laws, policies and institutions, which rules out laws that enforce segregation.

recognize-territorial-claims-from-conque.rationale: He calls Russia's invasion a blatant violation of international law and says any settlement must uphold Ukraine's territorial integrity within recognized borders.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He laments that regular migration pathways are becoming ever more restrictive and says migrants are being dehumanized for political gain.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He calls for reforming the international financial architecture so global financial institutions reflect today's world, with much stronger developing-country voice.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He says cuts in development aid are a death sentence for many and urges larger, more concessional finance for developing countries.

slavery-reparations.rationale: He has called for reparations for enslavement as part of reparatory justice.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He urged a solidarity or wealth tax on the rich who profited during the pandemic, citing a $5 trillion rise in the richest's wealth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He calls the invasion of Ukraine a blatant violation of the UN Charter and says peace must uphold territorial integrity within recognized borders.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In his 2025 priorities address he lists universal health coverage among the high-impact areas the world must accelerate.

universal-morality.rationale: He calls human rights universal, indivisible and interdependent.

women-suffrage.rationale: He calls for women's equal participation and leadership opportunities in political power and in peace processes.

notes: Searched, as the Secretary-General: climate, nuclear weapons and arms, the death penalty, LGBTQI+ rights, migration, Security Council reform, international law and the use of force, Ukraine, AI, finance and gender. Not yet searched: his record as Portuguese prime minister (1995-2002), his UNHCR years and his Socialist International presidency; statements that name no topic are null. As Secretary-General he speaks for a consensus of member states, so only statements he made in his own name are used.
